summary.text: Herbert C. Conaway Jr. is a physician and attorney and a former U.S. Air Force Medical Corps officer who represented Burlington County-area District 7 in the New Jersey General Assembly from 1998 to 2024, chairing its Health Committee, before winning election to Congress in 2024. He ran unopposed in the 2026 Democratic primary and is seeking a second term.

paragraphs.text: According to his House biography, he is a lifelong Burlington County resident and the son of a teacher and a nurse. He graduated from Bordentown Regional High School in 1981.
Earned a B.A. in politics from Princeton University in 1985, an M.D. from Jefferson Medical College in 1989, and a J.D. from Rutgers Law School, Camden, in 1996.

Served in the U.S. Air Force from 1992 to 1996, reaching the rank of Captain in the Medical Corps at McGuire Air Force Base, where his House biography says he worked as a general medical officer and rose to assistant director of the primary care clinic.

After an internal medicine residency, practiced in primary care settings and became a clinical professor at an inner-city community hospital, according to his House biography; Ballotpedia lists his professional experience as a private practicing physician and work at Cooper University Hospital.

Served in the New Jersey General Assembly representing District 7 from 1998 until his election to Congress in 2024, chairing the Health Committee and serving on the Budget, Appropriations, and Military and Veterans' Affairs committees.

His House biography credits him with sponsoring New Jersey's school funding formula and with legislation on public school nutrition, environmental protection, property tax relief, veterans' services, and public safety.
Won the open 3rd District seat in November 2024 with 53.2% of the vote over Republican Rajesh Mohan, succeeding Rep. Andy Kim, and took office in January 2025.

Serves in the 119th Congress on the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs (Subcommittee on Health and Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations) and the Committee on Small Business (Subcommittee on Economic Growth, Tax, and Capital Access). Advanced unopposed from the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary.
